title: Tocket the Thinking Goblin
markdown:
Snow-dusted summits of Gleamstone Country rang when the wind chose to be bells. Icy streams laughed down the rocks. In a moss house, goblin Tocket woke while the moon still made long shadows. A groan moved in his chest like pebbles changing their minds. He pulled a patchwork quilt—every colour, and a few that had not applied—tighter.

“Today,” he told the ceiling, “no volunteering. Not a solitary mandatory anything. Quiet. Personal projects.”

Tocket wanted warmth, a book with a spine that still argued, and the particular peace of not being pointed at. His finest skill was being just about to be volunteered. He had perfected the nap that began at the word task; the sudden study of a pebble that required three hills of distance; the urgent inspection of north-side moss, which took him conveniently far from circles and involved a notebook he never filled. Neighbours called it laziness. Tocket called it scheduling. Bracket, who had seen every schedule, called it nothing and stole a button.

Gruff, next door, was early and loud. His laugh was stones enjoying a slope. “Tocket! Up! Excellent. The Elder wants everyone at the Great Stone Circle. Gremlins. A terrible racket.”

Tocket’s large ears twitched. Gremlins. Racket. Volunteer. His stomach did a tadpole flop. “I was about to organise the sock drawer. Pairing prevents existential dread. Science.”

Gruff was already being towed by another goblin. “Brave souls, Tocket!” The boom faded. The buffer was gone.

Tocket slipped the back way, past the woodpile he had been meaning to stack since last frost and the sock drawer that was, in fact, a genuine catastrophe. Bracket, a glossy black crow, rode his shoulder, preened a feather that had ideas about shine, and tilted a knowing head. “Caw,” which in their private weather meant: trouble, and you are usually beside it, or leaving it by a scenic route.

“Observer today,” Tocket said. “Not participant.” He took the thin high trails, wind mournful, population low, goats like moving rocks. From there: a chittering din and clangs that had no manners, a rhythm that made the pines look embarrassed. The mountain was being disturbed on purpose. A hare sat up, judged the noise, and went back to being a hare. Tocket envied the career.

At the Stone Circle goblins packed themselves into bravery they had not scheduled. Someone had brought a frying pan, which was either a weapon or breakfast. The Elder stood on a raised rock, icicle beard twinkling as if wisdom had a temperature. “Peace is disturbed. Screeching Gremlins in the old Crystal Caves. We need volunteers to persuade them to leave.” A mutter went round: persuade, in goblin, often meant poke. Tocket’s hiding-pine smelled of sap and last year’s excuses. He stayed put and counted clangs the way other people counted coins.

Tocket, behind hardy pines, sweated in cool air. Persuade sounded like a fight wearing a hat. He would watch. He would think. Bracket was a dark quiet on his arm.

The gremlins were tiny, quick, eyes like jet, hands like trouble that had been given a drum. They were not biting. They were not throwing the Elder’s hat, which Tocket had half expected and half budgeted time to avoid. They were playing: metal scraps, waves of noise, bodies vibrating with joy, a concert that had not asked the valley. “Bored,” Tocket whispered. “They need a hobby.” Rhythm comforted creatures; a too-loud chime became the whole day, the way a dripping tap became a personality. One basin, large and hollow, dented by enthusiasm, took their favourite stones. That clang travelled furthest, found windows, found nerves, found the Elder’s beard. Remove that, and a clever goblin need not sweat, or volunteer, or invent a sock emergency. He sketched the plan on air. Bracket looked unconvinced, which was his usual review.

A shadow ate the sun. Damp moss and pine arrived in the air. Groll the Ogre Shepherd towered, crag face, moss tufts, eyes usually half-shut on shaggy goats and now sharp on Tocket. His staff could flatten a hut by accident.

“Skulking. The Elder wants volunteers, not furniture.”

Tocket’s heart performed gymnastics. Then he remembered the basin, and that Groll could see. “Not hiding. Strategising.”

“Strategising how to avoid work.”

“Strategising how to solve it without fuss. They love loud repetition. That basin is a dinner bell. Stop the clang…”

Groll’s eyes narrowed. He had seen Tocket avoid fences and water-buckets. This was different: thinking, offered like a tool. “How, little goblin?”

“Borrow the basin. If they grow bored, they wander. It is heavy for one, even a clever one.”

Groll stroked his chin, almost gentle. “Not afraid of gremlins. Afraid of being asked to fight them.”

“Something like that.”

An extra clang made Bracket jump. The crow dropped to shiny pebbles by Groll’s worn boots and set them skittering: clicks, a small storm.

“See,” Tocket said. “Goats and grass. Gremlins and shine. Divert them. I will push.”

Groll’s chuckle was a happy earthquake. “A diversion. Very well.” He hoo’d, vast. Birds left trees. The gremlins paused, jet eyes wide, curious as cats at a cupboard.

While the ogre occupied the audience—another hoo, a goat joke that the goats ignored—Tocket reached the cave mouth. Cold air, crystal glitter, the smell of old bangs. The basin gleamed dully and weighed like a grudge someone had stored for winter. He shoved. It complained. Desperation lent him a better back than the sock drawer ever had. Bracket flew ahead, beak-nudging when the rim caught on a lip of ice, a black comma of encouragement. They rolled it, inch by undignified inch, to a snowdrift that had been minding its own business, and buried the worst of the metal. Cold. Muffled. Tocket sat on a rock and discovered he had been brave in a sideways fashion, which was the only fashion he trusted.

The gremlins found their clang gone and Groll quiet. They chittered, uncertainty replacing hobby. A squirrel and a patch of bright berries won. They drifted. The village’s headache went with them.

The Elder emerged from an outcrop, bewildered. “The noise stopped. Where are the volunteers?”

Groll nodded, slow, beside a breathless Tocket and a smug crow. “Solving. He is not as lazy as he looks. Indirect. Clever.”

Warmth spread that was not from heaving. Tocket had not shouted. The day was still, mostly, his. Moonlight later found a high rope bridge and made it silver. “If you are going to be mysterious,” he told Bracket, “be punctual with the pebbles. You threw the timing.” Bracket ruffled, which was agreement and no apology. Tocket went home to the sock drawer and, for once, left it messy on purpose. Quiet had been earned, not dodged.
